content: 1. For patients weighing ≤36 kg, the use of this medication is not recommended due to the lack of a suitable formulation. 2. For patients weighing ≥36 kg, the recommended dose is 500 mg orally every 12 hours, co-administered with ritonavir 200 mg orally every 12 hours (boosted therapy). Administration with ritonavir is essential to achieve proper dosing and maintain adequate blood levels. 3. No dose adjustment is necessary for patients with mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class A). 4. For patients with moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class B or C), concurrent use is contraindicated. 5. This medication is indicated for the treatment of HIV-1-infected patients who are treatment-experienced and infected with HIV-1 strains resistant to more than one protease inhibitor. It must be used with ritonavir in addition to other antiretrovirals. 6. For children under 2 years of age, safety and efficacy have not been established. 7. For children aged ≥2 years and weighing <36 kg, the medication is not recommended due to the lack of a suitable pediatric formulation. 8. For children aged ≥2 years and weighing ≥36 kg, the recommended dose is 14 mg/kg plus ritonavir 6 mg/kg orally every 12 hours, or 375 mg/m² plus ritonavir 150 mg/m² orally every 12 hours. The dose should not exceed the adult dose of 500 mg plus ritonavir 200 mg orally every 12 hours. Administration with ritonavir is essential to achieve proper dosing and maintain adequate blood levels. Drug Interactions: 9. Tipranavir increases the levels of alfuzosin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for increased toxicity. 10. Tipranavir increases the levels of alprazolam by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for increased toxicity. 11. Tipranavir increases the levels of amiodarone by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Tipranavir increases the levels of aprepitant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Tipranavir increases the levels of atorvastatin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the increased risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Tipranavir increases the levels of cobimetinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Tipranavir increases the levels of conivaptan by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Tipranavir increases the levels of dihydroergotamine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Tipranavir increases the levels of intranasal dihydroergotamine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Tipranavir increases the levels of elbasvir/grazoprevir by other mechanisms (see comment). This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of ALT elevations caused by increased grazoprevir plasma concentrations. 20. Tipranavir increases the levels of eletriptan by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for increased toxicity. 21. Tipranavir increases the levels of eliglustat by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated with eliglustat in poor or intermediate metabolizers. 22. Tipranavir increases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF. This combination is contraindicated as elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be administered with other antiretrovirals. 23. Tipranavir increases the levels of enzalutamide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Tipranavir increases the levels of eplerenone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 25. Tipranavir increases the levels of ergoloid mesylates by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 26. Tipranavir increases the levels of ergonovine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Tipranavir decreases the levels of etravirine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it may result in a significant decrease in plasma concentrations of etravirine and loss of therapeutic effect. 28. Tipranavir increases the levels of finerenone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Tipranavir increases the levels of flecainide by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QT prolongation. 30. Tipranavir increases the levels of flibanserin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 31. Tipranavir increases the levels of fosaprepitant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Tipranavir increases the levels of indinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 33. Tipranavir increases the levels of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Tipranavir increases the levels of ivabradine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 35. Tipranavir decreases the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated as it decreases sofosbuvir levels and its active metabolite responsible for pharmacologic effects. 36. Tipranavir increases the levels of lomitapide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to significantly increased levels. 37. Tipranavir increases the levels of lonafarnib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 38. Tipranavir increases the levels of lopinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 39. Tipranavir increases the levels of lovastatin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the increased risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 40. Tipranavir increases the levels of lurasidone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 41. Tipranavir increases the levels of mavacamten by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of heart failure caused by systolic dysfunction. 42. Tipranavir increases the levels of methylergonovine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 43. Tipranavir increases the levels of methylprednisolone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 44. Tipranavir increases the levels of naloxegol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of opioid withdrawal symptoms. 45. Tipranavir increases the levels of nelfinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 46. Tipranavir increases the levels of pacritinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 47. Tipranavir increases the levels of pimozide by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. 48. Tipranavir increases the levels of propafenone by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 49. Tipranavir increases the levels of quinidine by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 50. Tipranavir increases the levels of regorafenib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 51. Rifampin decreases the levels of tipranavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it may result in loss of antiviral efficacy and/or development of viral resistance. 52. Tipranavir increases the levels of simvastatin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the increased risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 53. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels of tipranavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 54. Tipranavir increases the levels of triazolam by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 55. Tipranavir increases the levels of venetoclax by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used after the ramp-up phase, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 75%. 56. Tipranavir increases the levels of voclosporin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 57. Tipranavir increases the levels of acalabrutinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 58. Tipranavir increases the levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration due to increased DM1 exposure and toxicity. 59. Tipranavir decreases the levels of afatinib by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration. If chronic therapy with a P-gp inducer is required, increase the afatinib dose by 10 mg daily as tolerated. 60. Apalutamide decreases the levels of tipranavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 61. Tipranavir increases the levels of aripiprazole by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 62. Tipranavir increases the levels of atazanavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 63. Tipranavir increases the levels of avanafil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration due to the risk of severe adverse events, including hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. 64. Tipranavir increases the levels of avapritinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 65. Tipranavir increases the levels of axitinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. If unavoidable, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. 66. Tipranavir increases the levels of bedaquiline by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefit outweighs the risk. 67. Tipranavir increases the levels of bosentan by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 68. Tipranavir increases the levels of bosutinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration due to a ~5-fold increase in bosutinib plasma concentration. 69. Tipranavir increases the levels of brigatinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. If unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by 50%.
